newsitem.title: USA: N. Korea to decide soon on peace talks. [CORRECTED 03:00 GMT 8/4]
newsitem.headline: N. Korea to decide soon on peace talks. [CORRECTED 03:00 GMT 8/4]

text.p: Amid a growing sympathetic international response to its severe food shortages, North Korea has told the United States it will soon decide whether to enter peace talks with rival South Korea, U.S. officials said on Monday.

One official said the Clinton administration believed Pyongyang has been positively influenced by the "cumulative affect" of recent food aid appeals for North Korea and was optimistic the Stalinist regime will agree to enter the talks.

In another major assist for Pyongyang, the giant grain trader Cargill Inc. announced on Monday it had reached agreement with the North Koreans on Saturday for an undisclosed amount of U.S. wheat, marking its first commercial sale of American grain to the regime (corrects to indicate not first U.S. sale ever, only with regard to Cargill).

"The North Koreans indicated that they will soon give the United States and the Republic of Korea a formal response to our joint briefing" proposal on peace talks, State Department spokesman Nicholas Burns told a news briefing.

Pyongyang communicated this view when U.S., North Korean and South Korean diplomats met in New York last Friday. "Our hope, of course, is that the North Koreans will agree (to) the four-party proposal themselves and that those talks can be begun," Burns said.

Asked about a statement by a South Korean foreign ministry spokesman on Monday that North Korea had asked for a second briefing on the proposal, Burns said: "We've had a lot of briefings. We're willing to have another, I guess, but we'd really like the North Koreans to accept the proposal."
The United States and South Korea launched a year ago an initiative for negotiations on a peace treaty formally ending the 1950-53 Korean War. China would also participate.

But the initiative lagged as the infiltration of a North Korean submarine into the south last September and North Korea's severe food problems worsened the already tense and complicated situation on the Korean peninsula.

The submarine incident was defused in December when North Korea apologised and agreed to attend a formal "briefing" on the peace talks proposal, which U.S. and South Korean officials provided in New York on March 5.

The food problem caused cash-strapped Pyongyang to plead for international donations and commercial barter deals. There were indications Pyongyang thought it was promised more food aid than initially received in return for attending a briefing.
North Korea suffered terrible food shortages after two consecutive years of crop-killing floods.

In a new burst of activity, the World Food Programme said last week it would double its latest appeal for food aid for North Korea to 203,000 tons. The United States has donated more than $16 million in food aid to the beleaguered nation, with the latest portion due to arrive there this month.

In addition, South Korean agreed to allow private donations of food to North Korea and an influential U.S. congressional delegation visited the North and publicly reported its views on the seriousness of the situation.

"I think everybody is getting more concerned that the crunch is really coming in North Korea and they are facing potential famine unless we all act very soon," said Michael Ross, spokesman for the U.N. World Food Programme.

The World Food Programme has determined North Korea needs 2.3 million tons of food this year. Pyongyang has said it could raise 1 million tons through commercial deals but the World Food Programme doubts that goal can be reached.
Ross said even if the Cargill deal goes through -- "and that would be welcome" -- the North Koreans "presumably still have a long way to go toward meeting the target."

The Korean Peninsula Energy Development Organisation, which oversees construction of two new nuclear reactors for North Korea under a 1994 deal with the United States, said a 55-member group of technical experts would be in North Korea on April 9-15 for talks in preparation for starting site work on the project soon.
